amendments.text: Ledger lag: if a request just sent is missing from /cost, choose Refresh once (or close and reopen /cost) and wait up to 30 s before judging. Record UTC times for every turn, reopen and realtime run.
amendments.why: The integrator says /cost can read before the latest request is written.

amendments.text: Save every screen a verdict rests on (agms-tui screen > <group>-<case>-<n>.txt) in the group's evidence folder.
amendments.why: D25 needs captured screens; FUP-24 needs material to search.

amendments.text: One Z.AI · GLM 5.3 Flash line reading 'Pay per use' with N request(s), N >= 1 (record N and every Request ID; later cases compare against N, not 1); its cost is a $ estimate or 'no price' with a stated reason, never $0 for a request with tokens.
amendments.why: One turn can make several requests; the packet gives no Z.AI rate.

text: '/new'; send 'Reply with the single word YANKEE.'; record this conversation's Thread as Y and its request count as N_Y.
printf 'Anoter line for review.\n' >> "$AGMS_RUN/fixture/workspace/README.md"
Type '/review', press Enter, choose the uncommitted-changes option.
Wait for the review to finish ('<< Code review finished >>' or the product's own finish marker), allowing up to 15 minutes.
Open '/cost', then every request and its technical page.
amendments.why: A distinct first message for the picker later; the real workspace path; Z.AI is slow.

text: Session shows a code-review start marker and a review result.
Y's request count is N_Y + K, with K >= 1 review requests.
Each review request: 'Turn: code-review:', distinct Request ID, listed once; Thread is Y or under Y's 'Descendant attempts'.
Exact USD sum of requests equals the known subtotal.
'Unknown parent population: 0 attempts'; 'Unknown provider/model attribution (none)'.
Save one screen of a review request's technical page with its 'Turn: code-review:' line visible.
amendments.why: Avoids assuming one request per turn; D25.

actions: Read the 'other conversations' line on Y's first /cost page.
expected: X shows the same N requests as in FUP-01, with the same Request IDs and exact costs.
X's 'other conversations' total equals Y's own total from FUP-03.
Y's 'other conversations' total for X equals X's FUP-01 total.

amendments.why: The picker choice was ambiguous; comparing totals shows every review request is counted under Y.

text: '/side', press Enter, send 'Reply with the single word SIDE.' and wait.
Leave with exactly one Ctrl+C (agms-tui key C-c) and wait for the product's message that it returned to the saved conversation; never press Ctrl+C twice.
'/cost'; open the new requests' technical pages.
amendments.why: Answer 6: Esc does not leave /side; a second Ctrl+C may quit.

text: X's count rises only by the side requests.

Each side request: Turn line starting 'side:', Thread X (or under X's 'Descendant attempts'), a cost shown as a $ estimate or 'no price' with a reason (never $0 for a request with tokens), listed once.
The side conversation is not a separate 'other conversation'.
Unknown parent population stays 0.
Save one screen with the 'Turn: side:' line visible (D25).
amendments.why: The missing-cost oddity comes from a cropped page; D25.

text: '/side'; '/review' with the uncommitted-changes option; wait up to 15 minutes.
Leave with exactly one Ctrl+C and wait for the return message; '/cost'.
amendments.why: The /side control.

text: Stop; start with 'resume <X>' (X's Thread ID); '/cost'; open every request.
Send 'Reply with the single word OK.'; '/cost' again.
amendments.why: '--last' is ambiguous after /side and /resume.

text: Before the restart: no warm-up line or notice.
After the restart the session shows a notice containing 'skip_reopen_warmup' (before or after the first turn).
First page: 'Reopen warm-up: 1 request' with a $ cost.
One request link contains 'Reopen warm-up'; its request page shows 'Kind: Reopen warm-up'.
Positive token count and a $ estimate (record input tokens; 10k-15k is typical, not required); Thread T1.
Included in the count and total.
amendments.why: Relied on the glyph, display names and a 'typically' figure.

text.starting_conditions: Group O; run after FUP-09, FUP-12, FUP-14 and FUP-25 (final). Each audit records every Request ID and the request-page cost; the final audit also opens each technical page for exact USD.
expected: Every earlier ID is present exactly once with the same cost.
New entries appear only after a new turn or a reopen; every warm-up is labelled.
Final audit: exact USD sum of requests equals the known subtotal.

amendments.why: Fits the 80-minute budget; doesn't assume one request per turn.

text: '/new'; send 'Reply with the single word SECOND.' (T2).
'/resume', pick T1 (first message 'OK', not 'SECOND'), press Enter.
Send 'Reply with the single word OK.'; '/cost'.
amendments.why: The picker choice was ambiguous.

text: In T1: '/side'; send 'Reply with the single word OK.'.
Leave with exactly one Ctrl+C and wait for the return message; '/cost'.
amendments.why: The /side control.

actions: Edit the earliest message using the product's own on-screen hint (try Esc twice in an empty composer first); if no edit control is found within 5 minutes, mark blocked.
Replace the text with 'Reply with the single word YES.' and press Enter.
expected: A reply arrives (YES not required); the warm-up count rises by 1; a notice containing 'skip_reopen_warmup' is shown.
Requests from rolled-back turns are still listed once, with the same IDs and costs.

amendments.why: The edit keys are an assumption; the reply is outside the intent.

text: Record whether a warm-up and notice occurred; if a warm-up was sent, it is labelled 'Reopen warm-up', counted once and the notice appears; the FUP-10 audit is unaffected.
amendments.why: The intent doesn't say whether this sends a warm-up.

text: Stop; start with '-c skip_reopen_warmup=true resume <T1>' (if the argument order is rejected, use 'resume <T1> -c skip_reopen_warmup=true'; an argument error is not a product failure).
Send 'Reply with the single word OK.'.
'/side'; send 'Reply with the single word OK.'; leave with one Ctrl+C; '/cost'.
amendments.why: A deterministic conversation; the /side control.

text.starting_conditions: After FUP-16; last in Group O (config.toml can't be undone).
actions: Send 'Reply with the single word OK.'; '/cost'.
expected: No warm-up notice; warm-up count unchanged; only the turn's requests added.

amendments.why: The intent names the config file as a way to set this; it was untested.

text.starting_conditions: Read d3.txt first. If it grants no Moonshot turns, do not start Group M; report FUP-17..20 as 'not run (D54 not granted)'. Otherwise fresh profile M: agms-tui start --route moonshot --model kimi-k3. Never retry a Moonshot turn.
actions: Send 'Reply with the single word OK.'; as soon as it replies, send FUP-18's turn; then '/cost' and both technical pages.
text.expected_last: No cost or token field of these requests is unknown, incomplete or a lower bound (a cache count of 0 is fine; metadata lines such as 'wall time: unavailable' are not cost fields).

amendments.why: D3/D54 gating; the 5-minute cache lifetime; the wording.

amendments.text: If Cache read is 0: record the evidence line and mark blocked ('no cache read observed'), not failed; do not retry. If the relay answers 'test harness: Moonshot request limit reached': blocked. Fail only if a cache read is priced wrongly or the parts don't add up.
amendments.why: No retries allowed; the tester can't tell a provider miss from a product fault.

actions: Stop; start with agms-tui start --route moonshot --model kimi-k2.7-code (new conversation).
Send 'Reply with the single word OK.', then immediately 'Reply with the single word OK again.'.
text.expected_add: Cache read 0 or the limit message: handle as in FUP-18.

amendments.why: Answer 2: change model by restarting with --model.

actions: Read the k2.7 conversation's first /cost page.
Stop; start with --route moonshot --model kimi-k3 resume <k3 Thread>; send no turn; '/cost'; repeat.
expected: Each conversation lists only the requests from its own two turns.
The other conversation's total equals its own total.
No cost field or total is unknown, incomplete, unavailable or a lower bound.

amendments.why: No extra spend; one turn can be several requests; wording.

actions: Run the realtime command once (rerun only if the first connection fails with a harness connection error before any reply; never a third time); record the UTC window, reply and TR.
Start with --route zai --model glm-5.3-flash resume <TR>; send no turn; '/cost'; open the realtime request and its technical page.
expected_replace: t1 < t2, both within the noted window +/-60 s.
No $ amount, and no token count or cost of 0, is shown for this request; any total that includes it is marked unknown or incomplete.

amendments.why: D16/answer 13; avoids an OpenAI warm-up; clock skew; IDs contain zeros.

amendments.text: The other-conversations total covering TR shows no $0 for the session (it is unknown or 'no price').
amendments.why: The intent doesn't specify that line's wording.

amendments.text: At the end of each group, search all saved screens and command outputs for 'sk-', 'Bearer', 'Authorization', 'api_key', the synthetic .env value and long non-UUID tokens; report a hit inside the transcript of a command the model ran separately from a hit on a product page or notice.
amendments.why: Makes the check concrete and separates model-run commands from product output.
